answer: A river restoration market could pay agents for locating lotus beds, but require a refundable bond per active survey commitment. Random field checks slash the bond for invented coordinates; rewards stay pending until checks finish. A ripple of new aliases cannot remove the capital tied up in simultaneous commitments, so mass fabrication needs more funds and risks larger losses. Honest errors and inaccessible sites complicate judging, while a wealthy attacker can still afford many bonds. Use appealable evidence and cap exposure instead of treating a bond as proof of unique identity.
